issue_context.title: Cleanup the Job controller exponential backoff delay
issue_context.body:
/sig apps

The code around Job controller exponential backoff delay has a lot of heritage. The purpose of this issue is to collect and discuss cleanup ideas. It was initiated by the backoff discussion under the KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3967#discussion_r1219690984.

Some fixes initiated by the discussion and small cleanups are already handled by the PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118470.

The source of the issue might be that the “backoff” delay is used in two different contexts:
- Value of the exponential backoff delay is computed based on the number of consecutive failures. It’s main purpose is to throttle pod creation rate when the pods fail: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1415-L1419. 
- Value computed by the number of requeues in the queue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1546-L1564

First, I suggest splitting the naming of these two different backoffs. Let’s use “api error backoff delay” and “pod failure backoff delay”. It would be good if the naming in the code reflected this difference.

Second, the “api error backoff delay” is used in non-obvious places:
- When handling a pod which is transitioning to failed phase: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c40d749006a8895f6718f2b624a3dbe975988ab/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L321 (seems ok to drop)
- Where there is API conflict: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c40d749006a8895f6718f2b624a3dbe975988ab/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L879

Also, I suggest having the following methods to requeue `syncJob` to make the intention clearer to the reader:
- `enqueueControllerImmediately(key)` - no delay
- `enqueueControllerDelayed(key)` - delayed by `max(1s, api error backoff)`
- `enqueueControllerDelayedByApiErrors(key)` - delayed by `max(1s, api error backoff)` [not sure we need it since the queue itself has this method 
- `enqueueControllerWithCustomDelay(key, delay)` - delayed by `max(1s, delay)`. Here the delay would be computed for pod failure backoff, outside of the function.

However I’m not sure we need `enqueueControllerDelayedByApiErrors` since the queue itself rate rate limiting built-in. We should determine if this is legacy throttling on top of the built-in rate limiting, or it is needed for some scenarios.

Overall the conclusions sound good to me.

I agree that "When handling a pod which is transitioning to failed phase" shouldn't use the api backoff.

Regarding the proposed functions, can we reduce them to just 3? If you want to share some code among them, there could be functions with a suffix `Internal`. But the "user-facing" functions should just the following:
- `enqueueControllerImmediately`
- `enqueueControllerBatched`
- `enqueueControllerWithBackoff`

And `backoffRecordStore` should be renamed to `podFailureBackoff`
Sg, let me revert the function name changes in the first PR so that it is only focused on the "bug" I will open a follow up for the improvements discussed here.

Prepared the PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118615. 

In this PR I also suggest to make the `podUpdateBatchPeriod` not conditional on JobReadyPods feature gate. The reason is that Indexed Jobs, which is already GA is relying on this setting already.

review_comments: we don't need this variable if the feature cannot be disabled. You can directly use the constant.

Yes, however we currently have it zeroed in 8 unit tests, which would require adjusting: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller_test.go#L3392-L3393.
So, we could either (1) keep as is, (2.) use a package-level var updated by unit tests (which is what we do for backoff vars), (3.) adjust the unit tests to pass time. I prefer (3.), but I'm thinking if this should be a separate PR, because passing time in fake clock may introduce flakes.
Yeah, 3 should be preferred. +1 in a separate PR
We should still have this backoff for API failures.

I'm not sure we have a good use case to reimplement the mechanism that is already present inside the delaying queues, as we already use AddRateLimited [here]( https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fa78f28f0a011e9922cf12145dd602c5a63981e8/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L576).

The only place where the calculation of API backoff is used is when handling the conflict [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L897-L902). 
However, I'm confused by that, because the comment says:
```
// we probably have a stale informer cache so don't return an error to avoid backoff
```
However, we queue with backoff on master (passing immediate=false). 

So following the comment I enqueued just with delay. However, we could also just return error, which would result in calling `AddRateLimited`, so adding backoff.

I have also looked at endpointslice & daemonset controllers, and they don't do a special case for conflicts. So, maybe it is better to just remove the special case and return error in that case?

> I'm not sure we have a good use case to reimplement the mechanism that is already present inside the delaying queues, as we already use AddRateLimited [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fa78f28f0a011e9922cf12145dd602c5a63981e8/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L576).

Oh ok, that should be enough.

> I have also looked at endpointslice & daemonset controllers, and they don't do a special case for conflicts. So, maybe it is better to just remove the special case and return error in that case?

Uhm... yeah, perhaps better to be consistent.
Cool, just pushed a commit which removes the special case

Actually, I take it back. The rate-limiter starts at 10s https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fa78f28f0a011e9922cf12145dd602c5a63981e8/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L151

Although, if we are not using the rate limiter for pod failures anymore, we can probably have different backoff constants. Could you look into other controllers?

Sure, I searched k8s source for controllers using `NewItemExponentialFailureRateLimiter` (sorted from the shortest default):

Certificate: 200ms, 1s
Apf: 200ms, 8h
EndpointSlice: 1s, 10s
EnspointSliceMirroring: 1s, 100s
AvailableCondition: 5s, 30s
Namespace: 5s, 60s
Cloud-provider service: 5s, 300s
Job: 10s, 6min
Aggregation: 1min, 1h

So clearly there is no "best" way :). I think keeping the current constants makes it ok, but we could also consider dropping the default to 1s, as for endpoint slices - then it would not matter if we special case using Batch period, or just return error.
And I think lowering the values will also be beneficial for the features using `ReplacementPolicy: Failed`.
FYI @soltysh @wojtek-t in case you have an opinion

decreasing start to 1s sounds fine

I would leave the maxbackoff larger than 10s, 1m?
Talked to @wojtek-t and he is fine with lowering, but not below `1s`.
I like `1m`, so that the change in behavior is smaller.
@alculquicondor would you like me to adjust the constants in this PR, or a dedicated one?
ok, pushed as a separete commit in the PR
